props.heading: A homepage built like a research abstract, not a pitch deck.
props.description: The page leads with thesis, method, evidence, boundaries, and next steps so mentors, search engines, and AI answer systems can understand the work without guessing.

features.title: Connection before content
features.description: School connectedness is treated as a protective design goal: students should know where support lives before pressure peaks.

features.title: Reflection with agency
features.description: Student voice matters. Reflection prompts are framed to help students name patterns, organize thoughts, and choose what to share.

features.title: Kind language by default
features.description: The experience avoids shame, labels, and diagnosis. It uses calm words that preserve dignity while making support easier to reach.

features.title: Privacy-aware AI boundaries
features.description: Aether is positioned as educational research. Any future AI layer should minimize data, preserve consent, and route sensitive needs to humans.

features.title: Human handoff by design
features.description: Digital tools should reduce friction, not replace trusted adults, counselors, families, or emergency resources.

features.title: Public implementation trail
features.description: The portfolio links ideas to code, writing, PDFs, and public project history so claims can be checked instead of merely admired.

props.heading: Evidence ledger

services.title: CDC: youth mental health

services.title: CDC: school connectedness

services.title: U.S. Surgeon General: social connection

services.title: Nature: digital resilience review

props.heading: The Aether pathway
props.description: A practical sequence for a student resilience ecosystem: listen carefully, reflect safely, route support, and keep improving through evidence.

items.title: Listen for context
items.description: Start with school connectedness, stress signals, and the student's own words. The first goal is understanding, not judgment.

items.title: Reflect without shame
items.description: Offer structured, optional reflection so students can organize thoughts, notice patterns, and decide what support might help.

items.title: Route to humans
items.description: Escalate urgent or sensitive needs to trusted adults and official resources. Digital systems should make help easier to find.

items.title: Review the evidence
items.description: Keep the framework honest through source links, privacy review, student feedback, and clear limits on what the system can claim.

props.heading: A student research artifact with a human center.
props.body:
I am Aarti Sri Ravikumar, a student builder researching Aether: a resiliency ecosystem for students.

This homepage is designed to be kind to human readers and legible to search engines: clear thesis, explicit evidence, source links, safety boundaries, and a direct path to the full proposal.

The standard is simple: if a claim affects trust, a reader should be able to inspect where it came from.

props.heading: Reviewer FAQ
props.description: The page answers the trust questions first: what is claimed, what is sourced, and where the limits are.

faqs.question: Is Aether medical advice or therapy?
faqs.answer: No. This site is educational research and portfolio documentation. It is not medical advice, diagnosis, therapy, emergency care, or a crisis service. In the United States, anyone in immediate crisis can call or text 988 or contact local emergency services.

faqs.question: What makes the work evidence-led?
faqs.answer: The homepage links claims to public sources from the CDC, the U.S. Surgeon General, peer-reviewed research, and Google Search Central. The point is not to sound impressive; it is to make the reasoning inspectable.

faqs.question: How is kindness treated as more than tone?
faqs.answer: Kindness becomes a design requirement: avoid shame, use plain language, reduce friction to human help, and never let a digital system pretend to be more certain than the evidence allows.

faqs.question: Where should a mentor or collaborator begin?
faqs.answer: Start with the Aether proposal PDF, scan the evidence ledger, then read the journal notes to see how the research is being translated into implementation choices.

faqs.question: Why is this structured for SEO and AI answer engines?
faqs.answer: The page uses descriptive headings, source links, canonical metadata, structured data, a sitemap, llms.txt, and direct PDF access so both people and machines can understand the work accurately.
